summary: Return all root-to-leaf paths whose values sum to targetSum.
mainInsight: DFS with a single shared path list: append the node, recurse, then pop (backtrack). When a leaf's remaining sum is 0 record a COPY of the path.

approaches.name: DFS with path copies per call
approaches.summary: Pass a new list to each recursive call.

approaches.name: Backtracking with a shared path
approaches.summary: append / recurse / pop; copy only at solutions.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal pattern: copy only when a solution is found.

promptVariants: Which technique enumerates all root-to-leaf paths without copying at every step?
What is the backtracking pattern here?
options: Append the node, recurse, then pop it
cards.answer: Append the node, recurse, then pop it
cards.explanation: The shared list always holds the current root-to-node path.

promptVariants: Why must the recorded path be a copy (`path[:]`)?
What would the answer contain without the copy?
cards.answer: The same list object is mutated as the DFS proceeds; storing the list itself would make every stored path alias that one list, which ends up empty/only the last state after backtracking. Copying captures the path at the moment of the match.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Worst-case time (n nodes): ___
cards.explanation: Visiting is O(n); copying up to O(n) paths of length up to O(h) can be quadratic (e.g. ~n/2 paths of length ~n/2 in an adversarial tree).

promptVariants: What is the auxiliary space and what about the output?
Distinguish stack space from output space.
cards.answer: Auxiliary: O(h) for the recursion stack and the shared path list. The output can be large (all matching paths, each O(h)), which is usually excluded from the auxiliary analysis.

promptVariants: Walk through the append/pop around the recursive call and explain why `path = [root.val]` starts with the root.
cards.answer: Each child's value is appended before descending and popped after returning, so the list always equals the path from the root to the current node. The root is pre-seeded because the loop only appends children. remaining is the target minus the sum of the path so far including this node; a leaf with remaining 0 completes a valid path.
cards.explanation: Appending inside the callee (at entry) is an equivalent style.

promptVariants: What does the function return for an empty tree?
How is an empty tree handled?
cards.explanation: There are no root-to-leaf paths, so the result list is empty.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[[]]: That would claim an empty path exists.
